category_title: Students with low fine motor skills unable to use traditional drawing tools or computer mice
minimal_context: The student is attempting to draw geometric objects independently using a computer mouse.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's draw a square on the screen. Go ahead and use the computer mouse to draw the lines.

STUDENT: (Looks stressed) I have difficulties using a computer with a mouse. I am not an active user of computers.

TUTOR: Just give it a try and see what you can do.

STUDENT: (Attempts to move the mouse) I am less precise in determining the direction and intensity of the movement. I can't control the speed.

TUTOR: Keep trying to move it to connect the corners.

STUDENT: I cannot draw unaided. Can you just hold the mouse and draw it following my instructions instead?

options.A: Have students work in groups of five to six to develop a master list of shapes, then as a class agree on five drawing rules.
options.B: Compromise, negotiate situations, and share decisions and power with the student regarding the drawing task instead of imposing control.
options.C: Provide adjustments to the physical environment and individualized study plans supported by educational technology during geometry sessions.
options.D: Encourage 'tootling' (reporting prosocial behavior) by providing a collective reward for the geometry class when they reach a target number of 'tootles'.
